description: A window function's PARTITION BY and ORDER BY - in a SELECT item or inline in QUALIFY - may reference a SELECT-LIST ALIAS, not just a base column, because Snowflake resolves the alias to its defining expression. When that was not done, an aliased PARTITION BY collapsed every row into ONE partition, so a dedup QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY <alias>) = 1 wrongly kept a single row. Pinned over a plain alias, over a COMPUTED alias (the cloud-loader shape), on the window VALUE itself so the per-partition numbering is visible rather than just the surviving count, and on a window ORDER BY alias. The precedence rule is the one that keeps it honest: a BASE COLUMN wins over a same-named alias, so PARTITION BY name resolves to the column and gives three partitions rather than the one a constant alias would give. A plain base-column PARTITION BY rides along as the regression guard. Converted 1:1 from query/WindowPartitionByAliasTest (now retired); the Java asserted row counts, so the converted tests pin which rows.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, ts INTEGER)
SELECT id FROM (SELECT id, name AS nm FROM t QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY nm ORDER BY ts DESC) = 1) ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, ts INTEGER)
SELECT id FROM (SELECT id, LOWER(name) AS lo FROM t QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY lo ORDER BY ts DESC) = 1) ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, ts INTEGER)
SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY nm ORDER BY ts) rn FROM (SELECT id, name AS nm, ts FROM t) ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, ts INTEGER)
SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY neg) rn FROM (SELECT id, -ts AS neg FROM t) ORDER BY rn
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, ts INTEGER)
SELECT id FROM (SELECT id, 'X' AS name FROM t QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY name ORDER BY id) = 1) ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, ts INTEGER)
SELECT id FROM t QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY name ORDER BY ts DESC) = 1 ORDER BY id
